Subject: Re: rstan - erroneous object.size

 

Hi Chris,

 

I guess this might be due to there is an environment object in the stanfit object.  There isn't much in this environment, but it might result in other related environments (such as parent env) being saved when the stanfit object is saved.  I will take a look when I have some time. 

 

Jiqiang 

 

On Wed, Mar 18, 2015 at 3:07 AM, Chris Hansen <chris....@stats.govt.nz> wrote:

Hi Jiqiang

 

We’ve been playing around with the rstan package and have noticed something curious, and we thought you might have some thoughts.  We’ve noticed that object.size() seems to dramatically underreport the size of objects of type stanfit.  For example, I’ve fit a model and the resulting object is apparently 1.2Gb according to object.size().  However, doing saveRDS()  results in a file that is 9.7Gb, and even when the stanfit object is the only object in the workspace the reported memory usage is over 6Gb. 

 

So, is there any reason that you can think of as to why object.size() would underreport the actual size of a stanfit object so dramatically?  I’ve had a little scan via str and .Internal(inspect()), but it’s a pretty large and complicated object, so thought I’d check with the developlers first.  I initially thought there might be a memory leak, but if that was the case I would expect memory usage to be larger than expected, but not the size of serialzed objects (via save or saveRDS).

 

Any help you could provide would be much appreciated.

 

 

Cheers

 

Chris Hansen
